title: How to Build a Placement-Ready Resume as a Diploma Student
summary: A practical, step-by-step guide to building a resume that actually clears ATS screening and impresses recruiters.
content:
Start with a clean, single-column layout — many ATS parsers struggle with multi-column resumes. Lead with a short summary tied to your target role, followed by Skills, Projects, Education, and Certifications in that order for most diploma-level applications.

For each project, use the format: what you built, what tools you used, and one measurable outcome. Avoid vague statements like 'worked on a project' — be specific.

Finally, run your resume through the Resume Center's ATS Analyzer before submitting anywhere, and address every 'weak section' flag it raises.

title: Understanding Government Exam Cutoffs and How to Prepare
summary: What cutoffs actually mean, how they vary by category and exam, and a realistic preparation timeline.
content:
Cutoffs represent the minimum qualifying score for a given category and change every year based on the number of vacancies and applicant performance — never assume last year's cutoff guarantees this year's result.

A realistic preparation timeline for most SSC/Banking exams is 6-9 months of consistent daily practice, split roughly 40% Quantitative Aptitude, 30% Reasoning, 20% English, 10% General Awareness for most exams — adjust based on your personal weak areas.

title: The Diploma-to-Core-Engineering Career Roadmap
summary: A realistic path from diploma graduation to a core engineering role, including GATE/PSU options.
content:
Diploma holders in Mechanical, Civil, or Electrical branches have three broad paths: (1) direct core-industry roles via campus placement, (2) PSU roles via GATE score, or (3) further studies via lateral entry into a B.Tech program.

If targeting PSUs, start GATE preparation at least 8-10 months in advance — it's a rigorous exam. If targeting direct industry roles, prioritize hands-on CAD/tool proficiency and at least one real or simulated design project.

title: Freelancing as a Diploma Graduate: Getting Your First 5 Clients
summary: A practical approach to landing your first freelance clients without prior experience.
content:
Your first clients rarely come from cold outreach — they usually come from your existing network (friends, family, local businesses) or from doing 2-3 free/discounted 'portfolio projects' to build proof of work.

Once you have 2-3 real examples, create a simple portfolio page and start applying selectively on freelance platforms, always tailoring your pitch to the specific job rather than sending a generic message.

title: What Recruiters Actually Look for in a Technical Interview
summary: Beyond correct answers — what separates a strong technical interview performance from a weak one.
content:
Recruiters consistently report that HOW a candidate thinks through a problem matters more than whether they arrive at the exact right answer instantly. Talk through your reasoning out loud, state your assumptions, and don't go silent when stuck — ask clarifying questions instead.

Also common: candidates who can't explain their own listed skills/projects in depth. Only list what you can defend in detail under follow-up questions.
